subject: Hosted API: persistent p99/p95 spikes on 32k-context requests (urgent)
messages:
From: Protonix Ops <ops@protonix.com>

Cc: Tom Keller <tom.keller@protonix.com>
Date: 2029-04-10T08:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API - intermittent p99 spikes on large prompts

Michael —

We started seeing sustained p95/p99 latency regressions this morning on several production jobs that use ~32k token context windows. Symptoms:
- p95 jumped from ~400ms to 1.8s across the board, p99s to 12s+.
- Sporadic 5xx errors (mostly 502/504) during long-generation tails.
- Throughput for those tenants dropped ~40%.

We collected a few short error dumps and an example request/response pair — attached as protonix_error_snippets.txt. Impacting critical customer flows for Protonix Health; their ops team is requesting immediate mitigation or a rollback to pre-4/9 kernel.

Can your team confirm a priority action plan? We’re also happy to join a call right away.

—Aisha

Attachment: protonix_error_snippets.txt (text)

On Tue, 2029-04-10 at 08:35, Michael Grant wrote:
> Thanks Aisha — I see this and I appreciate the attachments. I’m escalating...

Initial diagnostic (quick notes):
- Observed increased tail latency correlating tightly with requests that use 24k-32k context windows.
- KV cache miss rate for those tenants jumped ~3x; effective batch sizes dropped due to serialization of long KV writes.
- Recent kernel selector change deployed 04/09 introduced a code path that defers certain attention-slicing optimizations for very long sequences; that increases CPU-side scheduling pressure for tails.

I attached a short trace sample (trace_sample_32k.json). Immediate mitigations we can apply (low-risk):
1) Per-tenant model fallback: route Protonix to the pre-4/9 model runtime (reduces throughput but safe).
2) Enable aggressive prefix/KV caching (edge cache + local shard) for Protonix to reduce recompute on repeated prefixes.
3) Temporarily limit maximum concurrent long-context slots per-worker for that tenant to prevent head-of-line blocking.

Longer-term: revert the attention deferral for long windows and iterate the kernel to avoid the serialization hotspot. I want to run a small canary for the rollback.

—Grace

Attachment: trace_sample_32k.json (trace snippet)

Thanks Grace. We’re seeing 502s as well (not just slow tails) — customer-facing pipelines are failing intermittently when the generation crosses ~28k tokens.

Immediate asks from our side:
- Can you flip the per-tenant fallback now while you investigate? Our production demand can't tolerate multiple-minute p99s.
- We need a formal timeline for rollback or a hotfix and an estimate for SLA credits (we will escalate internally if we do not get a satisfactory remedy).

We’re available for a call now.

—Aisha
From: Laura Bennett <laura@redwood.ai>

Aisha — sorry for the impact. I’ve opened incident INC-20290410-PX and shared an initial status note to Protonix execs. Summary of actions taken:
- Activated tenant routing to pre-4/9 runtime (rolled back for Protonix) at 09:22 PT; monitoring in progress.
- Enabled aggressive prefix caching for Protonix reads.
- Increased concurrent long-window worker pool for Protonix by +20% to reduce queueing.

Protonix team: could you confirm whether error rates are improving? We will keep the rollback active while Grace validates the trace.

Attachment: mitigation_steps.md (summary of actions and rollback steps)

—Laura
